title: Generate and Heal Playwright Tests with Recorded API Traffic
summary: Use mock-lab and proxymock to generate a Playwright spec, record a passing replay, and repair a renamed button with the shop API stopped.
body_markdown:
The shop in mock-lab has a **Load items** button that fetches` GET /items` and displays apples and pears. In this walkthrough, you’ll use the shop’s recorded API response to generate a Playwright test. Then you’ll rename the button, watch the original test fail, and use proxymock to propose a repair. The shop API stays stopped throughout.


The exercise extends the existing[mock-lab browser journeys lab](https://github.com/speedscale/mock-lab/tree/main/labs/browser-journeys) . The[companion article](https://speedscale.com/blog/why-playwright-tests-need-api-evidence/) explains why a passing test can still be a bad repair.


## 1. Start the mock-lab storefront


Install[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 22 or newer, Git and Make.[Install and initialize proxymock](https://docs.speedscale.com/proxymock/getting-started/quickstart/quickstart-cli/) and use v2.5.1487 or newer. Ports 3000 and 4140 should be free. Leave the API on port 8081 stopped.


From the directory where you want to clone the repository, run:


```text
git   clone   https://github.com/speedscale/mock-lab.git
cd   mock-lab/labs/browser-journeys
make   install
proxymock   journeys   explore   --help
proxymock   journeys   heal   --help
make   site
```


Keep that terminal running. The site loads on` http://localhost:3000` . Its API calls target` http://api.localtest.me:8081` , a separate origin. The lab’s recording contains the first-page response, so skip` make api` and` make record` . If your network blocks DNS answers that point to 127.0.0.1, add` 127.0.0.1 api.localtest.me` to` /etc/hosts` , as the[lab README](https://github.com/speedscale/mock-lab/tree/main/labs/browser-journeys#what-is-here) explains.


Prompt for a coding agent


```text
Use the Speedscale mock-lab browser journeys lab at https://github.com/speedscale/mock-lab/tree/main/labs/browser-journeys. Clone it into an isolated directory and work in labs/browser-journeys. Verify Node 22+, Git, Make, initialized proxymock v2.5.1487 or newer, and that proxymock journeys explore --help and proxymock journeys heal --help both work. Run make install and start make site on port 3000 in a managed background process. Keep the shop API on port 8081 stopped. Use the committed recording. Report the commands and anything you could not verify.
```


## 2. Generate a Playwright test from the recording


Open a second terminal in` mock-lab/labs/browser-journeys` . List the recorded sessions and then generate the spec. The lab has one recorded item-list flow, so use the default session selection.


```text
proxymock   journeys   explore   --in   proxymock/recording   --list


proxymock   journeys   explore   \
--in   proxymock/recording   \
--url   http://localhost:3000   \
--out   proxymock/explored-journeys   \
--name   shop-items
```


Open` proxymock/explored-journeys/shop-items.spec.ts` . Look for the button click and the response wait for` GET /items` . The explorer starts its own mock and uses the recorded response to decide whether the click reached the target call.


Import` expect` alongside` test` at the top of the generated file. Inside the step for` GET /items` , add the following assertion after the response wait so the test also checks what a shopper sees.


```text
await   expect  (page.  getByRole  (  'listitem'  )).  toHaveText  ([  'apple'  ,   'pear'  ]);
```


Prompt for a coding agent


```text
From labs/browser-journeys, list sessions with proxymock journeys explore --in proxymock/recording --list. Explore the default session against http://localhost:3000 with --out proxymock/explored-journeys --name shop-items. Keep the local shop API stopped. Inspect shop-items.spec.ts and show the action and response wait for GET /items. Import expect and add a Playwright listitem assertion for apple and pear after the response wait. Keep the generated click and wait and tell me which recorded calls were reached.
```


## 3. Save a passing replay, then rename the button


In a third terminal in` mock-lab/labs/browser-journeys` , start the lab mock and leave it running.


```text
make   mock
```


Back in the second terminal, replay your generated spec. Keep the output directory including` browser-journey-results.json` and its recorded traffic. Heal uses them together to compare the original journey with candidate repairs.


```text
proxymock   replay   \
--in   proxymock/recording   \
--browser   proxymock/explored-journeys   \
--test-against   http://localhost:3000   \
--browser-proxy   http://localhost:4140   \
--out   proxymock/results/heal-baseline
```


Confirm the summary shows one passing journey before continuing. In` app/site/index.html` , change the text of the button with` id="load"` from **Load items** to **Load shop items** . Keep the button’s ID and event handler. Stop and rerun` make site` in the first terminal because the site reads the HTML at startup.


Replay again with a different output directory. This time, look for a timeout at the old locator. Keep the passing baseline for the next step.


```text
proxymock   replay   \
--in   proxymock/recording   \
--browser   proxymock/explored-journeys   \
--test-against   http://localhost:3000   \
--browser-proxy   http://localhost:4140   \
--out   proxymock/results/heal-before-fix
```


Prompt for a coding agent


```text
From labs/browser-journeys, start make mock on port 4140. Run proxymock replay against http://localhost:3000 with --in proxymock/recording --browser proxymock/explored-journeys --browser-proxy http://localhost:4140 --out proxymock/results/heal-baseline. Confirm one pass and keep the output with its traffic. Change only the id="load" button text in app/site/index.html from Load items to Load shop items, restart the site, and rerun the same replay to proxymock/results/heal-before-fix. Verify the original locator times out. Preserve the baseline and keep the shop API stopped.
```


## 4. Review and apply the proposed repair


From the second terminal in` mock-lab/labs/browser-journeys` , point Heal to the generated spec and the passing replay. Heal starts its own mock for these probes.


```text
proxymock   journeys   heal   \
--in   proxymock/recording   \
--browser   proxymock/explored-journeys   \
--url   http://localhost:3000   \
--baseline   proxymock/results/heal-baseline
```


Review` proxymock/journey-heal.diff` . The proposed change should replace the locator’s **Load items** name with **Load shop items** . Check that the response wait and the apple-and-pear assertion are intact. Heal accepts a replacement when the whole test passes and its API calls match the passing replay.


Patch paths are relative to the repository root. From the lab directory, run the following:


```text
git   -C   ../..   apply   --check   labs/browser-journeys/proxymock/journey-heal.diff
git   -C   ../..   apply   labs/browser-journeys/proxymock/journey-heal.diff


proxymock   replay   \
--in   proxymock/recording   \
--browser   proxymock/explored-journeys   \
--test-against   http://localhost:3000   \
--browser-proxy   http://localhost:4140   \
--out   proxymock/results/heal-after-fix
```


Look for one passing journey with the renamed button. Compare its` GET /items` call and list assertion with the baseline. Stop the site and the lab mock when you’re done.


Prompt for a coding agent


```text
From labs/browser-journeys, run proxymock journeys heal with --in proxymock/recording --browser proxymock/explored-journeys --url http://localhost:3000 --baseline proxymock/results/heal-baseline. Show me proxymock/journey-heal.diff and confirm it changes only the old button locator. Use the browser_journeys MCP heal action if available and display the returned diff. Once I approve the patch, check and apply it from the repo root. Replay through the lab mock to proxymock/results/heal-after-fix and confirm the test passes, GET /items is present, and the apple-and-pear assertion survives. Stop the site and mock you started, and report any skipped or failed steps.
```


## Frequently asked questions


### Do I need to run the mock-lab API?


Keep the lab API stopped. The frontend loads from its own local server, and proxymock answers the item request from the lab's committed recording.


### Why does Journey Heal need a passing replay?


Heal compares every candidate's calls with the newest passing replay for that journey. Keep browser-journey-results.json and the traffic files alongside it.


### Can I use a coding agent to generate and heal the test?


Yes. The proxymock MCP tool browser_journeys supports sessions, explore, and heal. The heal action returns a diff you can review and apply.
